lesson.subject: Mathematics
lesson.subtopic: Need for statistics: purposes, and the collection and tabulation of data

objectives.objective: analyse and interpret statistical data presented in tables

entry-behaviour.item: Students are familiar with counting and recording information.

materials.item: classroom register, bottle tops, pencils or counters.

references.item: New General mathematics for Junior Secondary school book 1 by MF Macrae page 157 – 171

activities.activity: asks questions such as how many boys and how many girls are in the class
answer, and the answers obtained are examples of data

step.title: Step 2 — the purpose and meaning of statistics
step.plan-content: Teacher introduces the concept of statistics as a method of collecting and organising information.

activities.activity: introduces the concept of statistics as a method of collecting and organising information

step.title: Step 3 — collecting, tallying and tabulating data
step.plan-content: Teacher takes the students through collecting data, recording it with tally marks, and setting it out in a frequency table.

activities.activity: takes the students through collecting data, recording it with tally marks, and setting it out in a frequency table

step.title: Evaluation
step.plan-content:
Assembled from the plan's own **Student Activity**, which between its three items covers both retained objectives. Her Evaluation line sets work from the textbook by reference — "Exercise 17a No 3 and 4 page 158 NGM" — so that question text is nowhere in the plan and cannot be coded. Her lettered markers are kept; nothing is renumbered and no wording is changed.
- (a) Define statistic - (b) State three methods of collecting data. - (c) Prepare a frequency table for the following data: 1, 1, 3, 4, 4, 3, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 1, 2.

questions.question: (a) Define statistic
(b) State three methods of collecting data.
(c) Prepare a frequency table for the following data: 1, 1, 3, 4, 4, 3, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 1, 2.
